description: Boolean indicator of whether the camera has infrared or low-light night vision capability for 24/7 surveillance. True indicates night vision support, false indicates daylight-only operation.

description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, or operational remarks about the camera (e.g., 'Requires manual cleaning monthly due to salt spray exposure', 'Shared coverage with camera STS-CAM-00124', 'Temporary installation pending infrastructure upgrade').
reference: Maximo Asset Management, Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP)

description: Current operational state of the camera in the surveillance network. reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 13.4, Port Facility Security Assessment (PFSA)

description: Type of electrical power supply for the camera. description: Primary shipping line or carrier operating the service. May be a single carrier or lead carrier in a vessel sharing agreement. Used for commercial relationship management and billing.

Email address of the Company Security Officer for security incident reporting and ISPS coordination.
Telephone number of the Company Security Officer for 24/7 security incident escalation.
Name of the designated Company Security Officer responsible for ISPS Code compliance and security management for the vessel. Required under SOLAS Chapter XI-2.
Maximum vertical distance between the waterline and the bottom of the hull (keel). Determines minimum water depth required for safe navigation and berth assignment.
Maximum weight of cargo, fuel, fresh water, ballast water, provisions, passengers, and crew that the vessel can safely carry. Expressed in metric tonnes.
reference: International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships

description: Unique seven-digit ship identification number assigned by the International Maritime Organization. Permanent identifier that remains unchanged through changes of ownership, flag, or name. Required for vessels 100 GT and above engaged in international voyages.
Unique IMO company identification number assigned to the ISM-responsible company.
Name of the company holding the Document of Compliance (DOC) and responsible for ISM Code implementation on the vessel. Identified on the vessel's Safety Management Certificate.

business_glossary_term: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Security Level
description: Current ISPS security level assigned to the vessel (1=normal, 2=heightened, 3=exceptional). Determines security measures and access control requirements during port calls.

business_glossary_term: Last Port State Control (PSC) Deficiency Count
description: Number of deficiencies identified during the most recent PSC inspection. High deficiency counts trigger increased inspection frequency and may result in detention.

business_glossary_term: Last Port State Control (PSC) Detention Flag
description: Boolean indicator of whether the vessel was detained during the most recent PSC inspection. Detention history is a key risk factor for future inspections.

business_glossary_term: Last Port State Control (PSC) Inspection Date
description: Date of the most recent Port State Control inspection conducted on the vessel. Used for risk profiling and inspection interval targeting under regional PSC MOU regimes.

description: Maximum length of the vessel measured from the foremost point of the bow to the aftermost point of the stern. Critical dimension for berth allocation and channel navigation clearance.

description: Nine-digit identifier used in the Automatic Identification System (AIS) and Digital Selective Calling (DSC) for vessel tracking and communication.
Measure of the cargo-carrying volume of the vessel, calculated by subtracting non-cargo spaces from GRT. Used for port charges and canal dues.
reference: International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships 1969

description: Current operational state of the vessel. Active indicates the vessel is in service and available for port calls. Laid up indicates temporary withdrawal from service. Under repair indicates the vessel is in drydock or undergoing major maintenance. Scrapped indicates the vessel has been decommissioned. Lost indicates the vessel has been destroyed or sunk. Detained indicates the vessel is held by port state control or other authority.
reference: Lloyd's List Intelligence Vessel Status Codes

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country where the registered owner is domiciled or incorporated. Used for sanctions screening and beneficial ownership analysis.

Code identifying the P&I club providing third-party liability insurance coverage for the vessel. Used for claims coordination and financial assurance verification.
Timestamp when this vessel record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

Unique IMO company identification number assigned to the registered owner organization. Enables corporate hierarchy tracking and sanctions screening.
Legal name of the entity holding title to the vessel as recorded in the ship registry. May differ from commercial operator or technical manager.

Composite risk score (0-100) calculated from vessel age, flag state, classification society, PSC history, ownership transparency, and sanctions screening. Higher scores indicate higher risk. Used for prioritizing inspections and service restrictions.
Date of the most recent sanctions screening check performed on the vessel and its ownership chain.

Result of sanctions screening against OFAC, EU, UN, and other sanctions lists. Cleared indicates no match. Flagged indicates potential match requiring review. Under review indicates active investigation. Blocked indicates confirmed sanctions match and vessel is prohibited from port services.
reference: OFAC SDN List, EU Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the nation where the shipyard is located.
Name of the shipyard where the vessel was constructed. Provides provenance and build quality indicators for risk profiling.
Unique IMO company identification number assigned to the technical manager organization.
Name of the company responsible for the technical operation, maintenance, and crewing of the vessel. May be the owner, a third-party ship manager, or the ISM company.
Maximum number of twenty-foot equivalent containers the vessel can carry. Applicable to container vessels only. Null for non-container vessel types.
Current registered name of the vessel as recorded in the ship registry. Subject to change through vessel renaming procedures.
reference: International Convention on Tonnage Measurement of Ships

description: Calendar year in which the vessel was constructed and delivered. Used for age-based risk assessment, PSC targeting, and insurance underwriting.

description: Sequential number indicating this port's position in the voyage's port call sequence. Used to order intermediate ports of call and support cargo routing logic.
Boolean indicator showing whether the cargo manifest for this voyage has been received from the shipping line. Critical for customs clearance, cargo planning, and terminal readiness.

Current status of customs clearance for the voyage cargo. Pending indicates awaiting customs processing, cleared indicates all cargo approved for release, inspection_required indicates physical examination needed, hold indicates customs detention, released indicates cargo available for delivery.

The estimated timestamp when the vessel is expected to arrive at the port. Updated throughout the voyage based on vessel position, speed, and weather conditions. Critical for berth planning and resource allocation.

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this scheduled port call was omitted or skipped by the vessel. Used for schedule reliability analysis and customer service impact assessment.

description: The number of laden (full) containers onboard measured in TEU. Used for cargo volume analysis and vessel utilization calculations.

Textual explanation for why a scheduled port call was omitted. Common reasons include weather delays, mechanical issues, insufficient cargo, port congestion, or schedule recovery actions.

business_glossary_term: OOG (Out of Gauge) Cargo Onboard Flag

Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, or additional voyage information not captured in structured fields. Used for inter-departmental communication and operational coordination.

description: Boolean indicator showing whether tug assistance is required for berthing and unberthing operations. Based on vessel size, maneuverability, weather conditions, and port regulations.

Current lifecycle status of the voyage. Planned indicates initial voyage planning stage, scheduled indicates confirmed berth and resource allocation, in_progress indicates vessel is actively executing the voyage, completed indicates voyage has concluded with vessel departure, cancelled indicates voyage was terminated before execution, delayed indicates voyage is behind schedule.

Classification of the voyage based on direction and scope. business_glossary_term: Actual Weigh Anchor Time (ATD - Actual Time of Departure from Anchorage)
description: Actual timestamp when the vessel weighed anchor and departed the anchorage position. Recorded by VTS for operational tracking and billing purposes.
Specific berth or position number within the anchorage area assigned to the vessel. Used for precise positioning and capacity management.
Priority ranking for the anchorage assignment used for sequencing and capacity management. Lower numbers indicate higher priority. Used by VTS to manage vessel traffic flow.

description: Expected timestamp when the vessel will weigh anchor and depart the anchorage. Used for berth planning and vessel traffic sequencing.

description: Government-issued identity document number (passport, national ID, seafarer's identity document) of the individual permit holder. Populated only when scope_level is 'individual'. Used for identity verification at port access control points and ISPS security zone entry. Classified as restricted PII.
reference: ISPS Code; IMO FAL Convention Form 5; ILO Seafarers Identity Documents Convention (No. 185); GDPR Article 9

description: Full legal name of the individual person (personnel, contractor, driver) who holds this permit or access credential when scope_level is 'individual'. Null for entity-level or vehicle-level accreditations. Classified as restricted PII as it directly identifies a natural person.
reference: GDPR Article 4; IMO Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006); ISPS Code; ILO MLC

business_glossary_term: Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Insurance Policy Number
description: The Protection and Indemnity (P&I) Club insurance policy number associated with this insurance certificate accreditation. Populated only when accreditation_type is 'pi_insurance_certificate'. P&I cover is a mandatory requirement for vessel operators and stevedoring companies operating within the port. Classified as confidential business data.
reference: International Group of P&I Clubs; IMO FAL Convention; SOLAS; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: The date by which the renewal application must be submitted to the issuing authority to avoid a lapse in accreditation. Typically calculated as a fixed lead-time before the expiry_date (e.g., 30 or 60 days prior). Drives automated renewal reminder workflows and compliance monitoring dashboards.
reference: ISPS Code; IMO FAL Convention; ISO 28000; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: Tracks the current state of the renewal process for this accreditation. Not Due indicates the document is current and renewal is not yet required. Renewal Initiated indicates internal renewal preparation has begun. Renewal Submitted indicates the renewal application has been lodged with the issuing authority. Renewal Approved indicates the renewed document has been received. Renewal Overdue indicates the document has expired and renewal has not been completed.
reference: ISPS Code; IMO FAL Convention; ISO 28000; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: The date on which the accreditation was formally revoked by the issuing authority or the port authority. Null when the accreditation has not been revoked. Used in audit trails and compliance investigations.
reference: ISPS Code; IMO Resolution A.1119(30); Port State Control (PSC) Authorities

description: Free-text description of the reason for revocation of the accreditation, as recorded by the revoking authority or port compliance officer. Null when not revoked. Critical for audit readiness and ISPS Code enforcement documentation.
reference: ISPS Code; IMO Resolution A.1119(30); ISO 28000

description: The Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tag number embedded in the physical access card or vehicle transponder associated with this accreditation. Used for automated gate access control and security zone entry tracking in NAVIS N4 gate operations.
reference: ISPS Code; NAVIS N4 Gate Operations; ISO/IEC 18000 RFID Standards

description: Indicates whether this accreditation applies at the entity (organisation/company) level, individual (person/personnel) level, or vehicle level. Drives compliance gating logic in PCS and VTMS workflows and determines which permit holder reference fields are populated.
reference: ISPS Code; Port State Control (PSC) Authorities; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: The date on which the accreditation was suspended by the issuing authority or the port. Null when the accreditation has not been suspended. Used in compliance investigations and audit trails to track the duration of suspension periods.
reference: ISPS Code; Port State Control (PSC) Authorities; IMO Resolution A.1119(30)

description: Free-text description of the reason for suspension of the accreditation, as recorded by the suspending authority or port compliance officer. Null when not suspended. Required for ISPS Code enforcement documentation and Port State Control audit readiness.
reference: ISPS Code; Port State Control (PSC) Authorities; ISO 28000

description: Official vehicle registration plate number for vehicle-level access permits. Populated only when scope_level is 'vehicle'. Used for automated gate access control, RFID matching, and port security zone vehicle authorisation in NAVIS N4 gate operations.
reference: ISPS Code; National Maritime Safety Authority; NAVIS N4 Gate Operations

description: Classification of the vehicle for which the access permit is issued. Populated only when scope_level is 'vehicle'. Determines applicable port zones, weight restrictions, and operational areas within the terminal. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: truck|trailer|forklift|reach_stacker|agv|private_vehicle|motorcycle|other — promote to reference product]
reference: ISPS Code; NAVIS N4 Gate Operations; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: Indicates whether the accreditation or document has been independently verified against the issuing authority's records. Unverified indicates the document has been received but not yet checked. Verified indicates successful confirmation with the issuing authority. Verification Failed indicates the document could not be confirmed as authentic. Pending Verification indicates verification has been initiated and is in progress.
reference: ISPS Code; WCO SAFE Framework; ISO 28000; Port State Control (PSC) Authorities

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each commodity handling authorization record. Primary key.

business_glossary_term: Commodity Handling Authorization - Commodity Code Id
description: Foreign key linking to the commodity code for which handling authorization is granted
User ID of the port authority or trade compliance officer who granted this authorization. Used for audit trail and accountability.

business_glossary_term: Commodity Handling Authorization - Port Community Participant Id
description: Foreign key linking to the port community participant who holds this commodity handling authorization
Date on which the commodity handling authorization was granted by port authority or trade compliance team. Used for audit trail and compliance reporting.
Current lifecycle status of the commodity handling authorization. Determines whether the participant is currently permitted to handle this commodity type through the port.

Reference number of the regulatory certification, license, or permit that supports this handling authorization (e.g., dangerous goods handling license, customs broker accreditation, quarantine facility approval). Links to external regulatory authority records.
System timestamp when this authorization record was created in the Port Community System.
Indicates whether this authorization includes permission to handle dangerous goods (IMDG class commodities). Requires additional ISPS and IMDG Code compliance certifications.
Date on which this commodity handling authorization expires and must be renewed. Port operations system enforces authorization validity before accepting cargo declarations.

Classification of the authorization scope. FULL = unrestricted handling, RESTRICTED = specific conditions apply, CONDITIONAL = requires additional approvals per shipment, TEMPORARY = time-limited trial authorization.
System timestamp when this authorization record was last updated. Used for change tracking and audit compliance.

Free-text notes capturing special conditions, restrictions, or compliance requirements specific to this participant-commodity authorization. Examples: 'Requires pre-arrival notification', 'Limited to containerized cargo only', 'Subject to quarterly audit'.

Maximum cargo volume in metric tonnes that the participant is authorized to handle for this commodity type per calendar month. Null indicates no volume restriction. Enforced by Port Community System for capacity planning and risk management.
Unique surrogate identifier for each location access authorization record. Primary key for the association.

User identifier of the port security officer or system administrator who approved this access authorization. Used for audit trail and accountability. References the identity management system user ID.

business_glossary_term: Location Access Authorization - Port Community Participant Id
description: Foreign key linking to the port community participant being granted access authorization

business_glossary_term: Location Access Authorization - Port Location Id
description: Foreign key linking to the port location for which access is authorized

Total number of successful access events by this participant to this location since authorization was granted. Incremented by gate control systems. Used for usage analytics and billing (if applicable). Reset to zero if authorization is revoked and re-issued.

Classification of the access permission level granted to the participant for this specific location. Determines operational privileges and security restrictions. Values: FULL_ACCESS (unrestricted operational access), RESTRICTED_ACCESS (limited to specific times/activities), ESCORT_REQUIRED (must be accompanied by port security), NO_ACCESS (authorization revoked but record retained for audit).
Timestamp when this access authorization was officially approved and became enforceable. Used for audit trail and compliance reporting. Must be on or before authorization_start_date.

Date on which the participants authorization to access this port location expires. Null indicates indefinite authorization subject to ongoing ISPS compliance. Gate systems automatically deny access after this date. Must be on or before the participants ISPS accreditation expiry date.

Date from which the participant is authorized to access this port location. Used by gate control systems to validate time-bound access permissions. Must be on or after the participants ISPS accreditation date.

Current lifecycle status of this access authorization record. ACTIVE = currently valid and enforceable, SUSPENDED = temporarily disabled pending investigation or compliance review, EXPIRED = authorization_end_date has passed, REVOKED = permanently cancelled due to security breach or contract termination, PENDING_APPROVAL = awaiting port security approval. Gate systems only honor ACTIVE authorizations.

Boolean flag indicating whether the participant is authorized to operate cargo handling equipment (cranes, reach stackers, RTGs) at this port location. Requires additional operator certification validation. Used by equipment management systems to enforce operational safety and authorization.

ISPS security clearance level required and granted for this participant-location combination. LEVEL_1 = normal operations, LEVEL_2 = heightened security threat, LEVEL_3 = exceptional security threat. Determines access permissions during different MARSEC (Maritime Security) levels. Participant must hold clearance at or above the locations current MARSEC level to gain access.

Timestamp of the most recent successful access event by this participant to this location. Updated by gate control systems upon each entry. Used for access pattern analysis and dormant authorization identification. Null if participant has never accessed the location since authorization was granted.

Time-of-day or day-of-week restrictions on when the participant may access this location. Format: JSON string or structured text defining allowed time windows (e.g., 'MON-FRI 06:00-18:00', '24/7', 'DAYLIGHT_ONLY'). Null indicates no time restrictions. Used by gate control systems to enforce temporal access policies.

Free-text explanation of why this authorization was revoked or suspended. Null if authorization_status is ACTIVE, EXPIRED, or PENDING_APPROVAL. Required for REVOKED and SUSPENDED statuses. Used for security incident investigation and compliance audits.

Boolean flag indicating whether the participant is authorized to bring vehicles (trucks, forklifts, terminal tractors) into this port location. False indicates pedestrian-only access. Used by gate lane systems to validate vehicle entry permissions.
Unique surrogate identifier for each participant trade exemption record. Primary key.

business_glossary_term: Participant Trade Exemption - Port Community Participant Id
description: Foreign key linking to the port community participant who holds the exemption or license

business_glossary_term: Participant Trade Exemption - Trade Restriction Id
description: Foreign key linking to the trade restriction for which the exemption or license is granted
Name of the government agency, regulatory body, or international organization that issued and approved the exemption or license.
Date on which the exemption or license was officially approved and granted to the participant.
Maximum volume, quantity, or value of goods that the participant is authorized to trade under this exemption. Unit depends on the restriction type (e.g., metric tons, TEUs, USD value).
Unit of measurement for the authorized volume (e.g., metric tons, TEUs, currency for value-based limits).
Detailed conditions, restrictions, and compliance requirements that the participant must meet to maintain the validity of the exemption.
Timestamp when the exemption record was created in the port community system.
Official reference number or identifier assigned to the exemption or license by the issuing authority. Used for verification during customs clearance and cargo release processes.
Current lifecycle status of the exemption. Determines whether the exemption can be used for customs clearance and cargo release decisions.
Classification of the exemption mechanism granted to the participant. Determines the scope and conditions under which the participant may conduct otherwise restricted trade activities.
Date when the exemption was last verified or validated by port compliance officers during a cargo clearance process.
Timestamp when the exemption record was last updated in the port community system.
Date on which the exemption or license expires. After this date, the participant is no longer authorized to conduct the specified trade activities without renewal.
Date from which the exemption or license becomes effective and the participant is authorized to conduct the specified trade activities.
Unique surrogate identifier for each port access permit record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this entity.

Foreign key linking to security.access_point. Business justification: Permits specify which access points holder may use for entry/exit. Essential for access control system integration and permit validation at gates. Role prefix clarifies this is authorized entry point,

Foreign key linking to safety.contractor_safety. Business justification: Access permits for contractor personnel must reference contractor safety qualification status. Permit issuance and renewal depend on current safety clearance, incident history, and training compliance

Foreign key linking to compliance.isps_facility_record. Business justification: Port access permits must validate against ISPS facility security requirements and current security level. Port security officers require this link to enforce zone access restrictions based on facility

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: ISPS security compliance requires tracking which port security officer issued each access permit. Critical for audit trails, security incident investigations, and regulatory inspections. issuing_offic

Reference to the port community participant entity (shipping line, freight forwarder, trucking company, port agent, etc.) under whose sponsorship this permit was issued. Links to the customer master.

description: Foreign key linking to masterdata.port_location. Business justification: Access permits grant entry to specific terminals, berths, or ISPS security zones; physical access control enforcement, gate validation, and security zone management require precise location-level auth

Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Vendors providing on-site services (equipment maintenance, construction, stevedoring) require ISPS-compliant port access permits for personnel and vehicles entering restricted zones. Real business pro
Time-of-day restriction applied to this permit. Unrestricted permits allow 24/7 access; other values limit access to defined operational windows. Enforced at gate entry systems and ISPS checkpoints.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP)

description: Reference number of the original permit application submitted through the Port Community System (PCS) or port authority portal. Links the issued permit back to the application workflow for audit and traceability.
reference: Port Community System (PCS); ISPS Code Part A Section 2

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) at which the permit application was formally approved by the issuing authority. Distinct from issue_date which records the calendar date of issuance. Supports ISPS audit trail with precise approval timing.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ISO 28000:2022

description: Date on which the security background check was completed for this permit holder. Used to determine whether a re-check is required at renewal based on the port's ISPS security policy interval.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; National Maritime Safety Authority Security Screening Guidelines

description: Outcome of the security background check conducted on the permit holder prior to issuance. Passed status is a prerequisite for active permit issuance under ISPS requirements. Waived may apply to certain visitor categories under escort.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; National Maritime Safety Authority Security Screening Guidelines

description: Physical badge or access card number printed on the permit holder's port ID badge. Used by gate access control systems, RFID readers, and security checkpoints to validate physical access. May differ from permit_number.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; Port Community System (PCS)

description: Unique reference token linking this permit to the holder's biometric record stored in the port's secure biometric identity management system (fingerprint, iris, or facial recognition template). The actual biometric template is NOT stored here — only the reference token. Null for vehicle permits.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; GDPR Article 9 (Special Category Data); ISO/IEC 19794 Biometric Data Interchange

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) at which this permit record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data governance and lineage tracking in the lakehouse silver layer.
reference: ISO 8601; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity and Accountability)

description: Identifier of the corresponding contact record in Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM for the permit holder or their sponsoring organisation. Enables cross-system traceability between the access permit and the CRM customer engagement record.
reference: Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM; Port Community System (PCS)

description: Indicates whether the permit holder must be accompanied by an authorised port escort at all times while within restricted ISPS zones. True for visitor and certain contractor permit types; False for credentialed personnel with full unescorted access.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP)

description: Calendar date on which the port access permit ceases to be valid. After this date the permit_status transitions to expired and physical access is denied. Renewal must be initiated before this date to maintain uninterrupted access.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ISO 28000:2022

description: Date of birth of the individual permit holder in yyyy-MM-dd format. Used for identity verification, background screening, and ISPS compliance records. Null for vehicle permits.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ISPS Code Part A Section 2

description: Name of the organisation that employs or sponsors the permit holder (e.g., shipping line, stevedoring company, customs broker, trucking company). Used to link the individual to their sponsoring port community participant for accountability and audit.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ILO MLC 2006

description: Full legal name of the individual permit holder (person) as it appears on their government-issued identity document. Populated for personnel, contractor, visitor, crew, and emergency permit types. Null for vehicle-only permits.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ISPS Code Part A Section 2; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006

description: The unique number of the government-issued identity document (passport number, national ID number, seafarer book number, etc.) used to verify the permit holder's identity during the application process.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; GDPR Article 4; IMO FAL Convention

description: Type of government-issued identity document presented by the permit holder at the time of application and verification. Used for ISPS compliance audit and background check records.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; IMO FAL Convention; ILO MLC 2006

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the nationality of the individual permit holder. Required for ISPS background screening and customs/immigration compliance reporting.
reference: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3; ISPS Code Part A Section 2; IMO FAL Convention

description: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code security level at which this permit was issued. Level 1 is normal operations; Level 2 is heightened threat; Level 3 is exceptional threat. Permits issued at higher security levels may carry additional access restrictions.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2.1; IMO MSC/Circ.1192; SOLAS Chapter XI-2

description: Pipe-delimited list of ISPS-designated restricted port zones to which this permit grants access (e.g., berth_side|container_yard|gate_complex|bonded_warehouse|control_room). Defined per the port's ISPS Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: berth_side|container_yard|gate_complex|bonded_warehouse|control_room|vessel_deck|hazmat_area — promote to reference product for zone management]
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2.1; SOLAS Chapter XI-2; IMO MSC/Circ.1192

description: Calendar date on which the port access permit was formally issued and became effective. Marks the start of the permit's validity period.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ISO 28000:2022

description: Name of the port authority department or designated security officer responsible for issuing this permit (e.g., Port Security Office, ISPS Compliance Unit). Required for audit trail and regulatory accountability.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: Maximum number of gate entries permitted under this access permit within its validity period. Null indicates unlimited entries (applicable to permanent and multi-entry permits). Enforced by the gate access control system.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; NAVIS N4 Gate Operations

description: Operational category of the permit defining its usage scope. Permanent permits are issued for long-term employees; temporary permits cover short-term contractors or visitors; single-entry permits are for one-time access events; multi-entry permits allow repeated access within the validity period.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP)

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique permit reference number assigned by the port authority at issuance. Used on physical badges, gate scanners, and ISPS audit trails. Format: PAP-<PORT_CODE>-<SEQUENCE>.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; IMO MSC/Circ.1192

description: Current lifecycle state of the port access permit. Active permits grant physical access; suspended permits are temporarily blocked pending investigation; revoked permits are permanently cancelled; expired permits have passed their expiry date without renewal.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; Port State Control (PSC) Inspection Guidelines

description: Classification of the access permit indicating whether it covers a person (personnel, contractor, visitor, crew, emergency responder) or a vehicle. Drives the applicable ISPS security zone rules and badge colour coding. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: personnel|vehicle|contractor|visitor|crew|emergency — promote to reference product if additional types are required]
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2.1; ISO 28000:2022

description: Permit number of the immediately preceding permit that this record renews or replaces. Enables lineage tracing across permit renewal cycles for ISPS audit and compliance history.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ISO 28000:2022

description: Free-text field for additional notes or special conditions associated with this permit (e.g., restricted to specific berth, requires safety induction completion, hazardous cargo handling certification required). Captured by the issuing security officer.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP)

description: Number of times this permit has been renewed since its original issuance. Tracks the renewal history for compliance reporting and to identify long-standing permit holders who may require periodic re-vetting under ISPS policy.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ISO 28000:2022

description: Date on which the permit was formally revoked prior to its natural expiry. Populated only when permit_status is revoked. Null for active, suspended, or expired permits.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ISO 28000:2022

description: Reason code explaining why the permit was revoked. Required when permit_status is revoked to support ISPS audit trails and incident reporting. description: Unique identifier of the Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) chip embedded in the permit holder's access badge or vehicle transponder. Enables automated gate entry/exit tracking and real-time zone monitoring within the port.

description: IMO vessel identification number of the vessel whose call is the basis for issuing this permit (e.g., for crew shore passes or vessel-specific contractor access). Null for permits not tied to a specific vessel call.

description: Date on which the permit was placed into suspended status pending investigation or administrative review. Populated only when permit_status is suspended. Null for all other statuses.

description: Free-text description of the reason for suspending the permit. Populated when permit_status is suspended. Supports security incident investigation and ISPS compliance audit.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 2; ISO 28000:2022

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) at which this permit record was last modified. Supports change detection, incremental loading in the lakehouse, and audit trail requirements.

description: Official government-issued registration plate number of the vehicle for vehicle-type permits. Null for personnel permits. Used at gate entry/exit for automated plate recognition and ISPS vehicle access control.

Name or role of the data steward responsible for maintaining and validating this IMDG classification master data. Typically the Safety & Compliance team or Dangerous Goods Compliance Officer.
Subdivision or division within the IMDG class (e.g., 2.1 for flammable gases, 3 for flammable liquids, 6.1 for toxic substances). Provides finer hazard categorization within the primary class.

EmS fire schedule code (e.g., F-A, F-B, F-C) specifying emergency response procedures for fire incidents involving this IMDG class. Referenced from the Emergency Response Procedures for Ships Carrying Dangerous Goods (EmS Guide).
reference: IMO EmS Guide - Emergency Response Procedures

description: EmS spillage schedule code (e.g., S-A, S-B, S-C) specifying emergency response procedures for spillage or leakage incidents involving this IMDG class. Referenced from the Emergency Response Procedures for Ships Carrying Dangerous Goods (EmS Guide).
reference: IMO EmS Guide - Emergency Response Procedures

description: Excepted quantity code (E0, E1, E2, E3, E4, E5) defining the maximum quantity per inner packaging and per package for excepted quantity shipments. Excepted quantities are subject to minimal regulatory requirements.
reference: IMO IMDG Code Part 3 - Excepted Quantities

description: Type or code of the hazard label required for containers and packages carrying goods of this IMDG class (e.g., 'Explosive 1.1', 'Flammable Gas', 'Toxic'). Used for visual identification and compliance with labeling regulations.
reference: IMO IMDG Code Part 5 - Consignment Procedures

description: Amendment cycle or version of the IMDG Code under which this classification is defined (e.g., 'Amendment 40-20', 'Amendment 41-22'). The IMDG Code is updated biennially; this field tracks which amendment cycle applies to this record.
Date when this IMDG classification record was last verified against the current IMO IMDG Code amendment. Used to ensure data currency and compliance with the latest regulatory requirements.

Maximum quantity per package or inner packaging that qualifies for limited quantity (LQ) exemptions under the IMDG Code. Expressed as a volume or mass (e.g., '1L', '5kg'). Limited quantities are subject to reduced regulatory requirements.
reference: IMO IMDG Code Part 3 - Limited Quantities

description: Indicates whether substances in this IMDG class are classified as marine pollutants under MARPOL Annex III. True if the class typically contains marine pollutants requiring special marking and documentation.

Reference to the applicable MARPOL annex for pollution prevention related to this IMDG class (e.g., 'Annex I - Oil', 'Annex II - Noxious Liquid Substances', 'Annex III - Harmful Substances in Packaged Form'). Used for environmental compliance and spill response planning.
Timestamp when this IMDG classification record was last modified. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
Free-text notes or additional guidance related to this IMDG class. May include port-specific handling instructions, local regulatory variations, or clarifications for operational staff.

Packing group classification (I, II, or III) indicating the degree of danger: I = high danger, II = medium danger, III = low danger. Used to determine packaging specifications and handling requirements.

Segregation group code assigned to this IMDG class for stowage and segregation purposes (e.g., acids, alkalis, ammonium compounds). Used to determine compatibility and separation requirements in vessel stowage planning and yard block allocation.
reference: IMO IMDG Code Part 7 - Stowage and Segregation

description: Reference to the segregation table in the IMDG Code specifying separation requirements (e.g., 'away from', 'separated from', 'separated by a complete compartment or hold from'). Defines minimum physical separation distances for safe stowage.
reference: IMO IMDG Code Part 7 - Segregation Table

business_glossary_term: Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) Regulation Reference
description: Reference to the applicable SOLAS Chapter VII regulation governing the carriage of this dangerous goods class by sea (e.g., 'SOLAS Ch.VII Part A', 'SOLAS Ch.VII Part B'). SOLAS Chapter VII addresses the carriage of dangerous goods in packaged form or in solid form in bulk.

Comma-separated list of special provision codes applicable to this IMDG class (e.g., SP23, SP172, SP274). Special provisions modify or supplement the general requirements for specific substances or articles within the class.
reference: IMO IMDG Code Part 3 - Dangerous Goods List Special Provisions

description: Stowage category code (A, B, C, D, or E) defining where this IMDG class may be stowed on a vessel. Category A = on deck or under deck; B = on deck or under deck with specific conditions; C = on deck only; D = on deck only with specific conditions; E = prohibited from carriage. Used in BAPLIE stowage planning.
reference: IMO IMDG Code Part 7 - Stowage and Segregation

description: Ending UN number in the range typically associated with this IMDG class. Defines the upper bound of UN numbers commonly classified under this hazard class.
reference: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

description: Starting UN number in the range typically associated with this IMDG class. UN numbers are four-digit identifiers assigned to hazardous substances and articles by the United Nations Committee of Experts on the Transport of Dangerous Goods.
reference: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

description: Effective start date for this IMDG classification record. Used to manage amendment transitions and ensure the correct classification rules are applied based on the cargo acceptance or vessel departure date.
Effective end date for this IMDG classification record. Nullable for current/active classifications. Used to manage historical records when IMDG Code amendments supersede or modify classifications.
Unique identifier for the packaging type record. Primary key.

Foreign key linking to masterdata.imdg_class. Business justification: Packaging types for dangerous goods reference IMDG hazard classifications to determine compatibility and handling requirements. Currently stores imdg_class_code as STRING; normalizing to FK allows joi
Self-referencing FK on packaging_type (parent_packaging_type_id)
Transport modes for which this packaging type is approved (e.g., sea, road, rail, air, intermodal). Multiple modes may be comma-separated. Used for intermodal logistics coordination.
reference: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

description: Timestamp when this packaging type record was first created in the master data system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Indicates whether cargo in this packaging type requires specific customs declaration or documentation beyond standard manifest entries.
Name or identifier of the business unit or individual responsible for maintaining this packaging type master data. Typically Safety and Compliance department.
Date from which this packaging type classification becomes effective and can be used in operational systems. Used for regulatory update management.
Date until which this packaging type classification remains valid. Null for currently valid records. Used for managing regulatory updates and deprecated packaging codes.
Indicates whether this packaging type can withstand fumigation treatment for quarantine and phytosanitary compliance without damage or contamination.
Recommended or required handling equipment for this packaging type (e.g., forklift, pallet jack, crane, Rubber Tyred Gantry (RTG), Mobile Harbour Crane (MHC)). Multiple types may be comma-separated.
External height dimension of the packaging in millimeters. Used for stowage planning and container loading optimization.

business_glossary_term: International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Packing Group
description: IMDG packing group compatibility indicating the degree of danger: I (high danger), II (medium danger), III (low danger), or not applicable for non-dangerous goods packaging.

business_glossary_term: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) Standard Version
description: Version of the ISO standard this packaging type conforms to (e.g., ISO 3394:2012, ISO 9711:1990). Used for compliance verification and audit trails.
Timestamp when this packaging type record was last updated. Used for change tracking and synchronization with downstream systems.
External length dimension of the packaging in millimeters. Used for stowage planning and container loading optimization.
Indicates whether this packaging type meets MARPOL requirements for prevention of marine pollution, particularly relevant for hazardous substance packaging.

Primary material composition of the packaging (e.g., steel, aluminium, wood, fibreboard, plastic, textile, composite). Critical for IMDG compliance and handling requirements. reference: IMDG Code - International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code

description: Maximum volumetric capacity of the packaging in liters. Used for liquid and bulk cargo capacity planning and compliance verification.
Maximum allowable gross weight (packaging plus contents) in kilograms. Critical for Safe Working Load (SWL) compliance and handling equipment selection.
Maximum number of units that can be safely stacked vertically. Null if not stackable. Used for warehouse and yard stacking operations.
Free-text field for additional remarks, clarifications, or operational notes related to this packaging type. Used for capturing context not covered by structured fields.
Current operational status of this packaging type in the master data system. Controls whether the packaging type can be used in new cargo bookings and manifests.

High-level classification of the packaging type for operational grouping and handling instructions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: drum|box|bag|crate|ibc|cylinder|jerrycan|pallet|composite|bulk|other — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Full descriptive name of the packaging type (e.g., Steel Drum, Fibreboard Box, Intermediate Bulk Container, Wooden Crate, Plastic Jerrycan, Gas Cylinder, Pallet).
Indicates whether this packaging type is suitable for use in refrigerated containers for temperature-controlled cargo.
Frequency and schedule of regulatory updates for this packaging type (e.g., biennial UN update, annual IMDG amendment). Used for compliance calendar management.
reference: UN Recommendation 21, IMDG Code Amendment Procedures

description: Segregation group code for dangerous goods stowage planning. Defines which other packaging types or cargo classes this packaging must be segregated from during transport and storage.

business_glossary_term: Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) Verified Gross Mass (VGM) Applicable
description: Indicates whether SOLAS VGM verification requirements apply to cargo shipped in this packaging type. Mandatory for containerized cargo under SOLAS Convention.
Free-text field capturing any special handling, stowage, or operational instructions specific to this packaging type (e.g., keep upright, fragile, protect from moisture, segregation requirements).
Indicates whether this packaging type can be safely stacked during storage and transport. Critical for yard management and Container Freight Station (CFS) operations.
Empty weight of the packaging itself in kilograms, excluding contents. Used for net weight calculations and cargo documentation.
Internal tariff code used for billing and Terminal Handling Charge (THC) calculation. Links packaging type to applicable port tariff schedules.

Standard UN packaging code as defined by UN Recommendation 21 for dangerous goods transport. Two to four character alphanumeric code identifying the packaging type (e.g., 1A for steel drum, 4G for fibreboard box).
reference: UN Recommendation 21 - Codes for Types of Cargo, Packages and Packaging Materials

description: Version of UN Recommendation 21 or UN Model Regulations this packaging type is classified under. Updated biennially to reflect regulatory changes.
Indicates whether this packaging type requires UN performance testing and certification for dangerous goods transport under IMDG regulations.
External width dimension of the packaging in millimeters. Used for stowage planning and container loading optimization.
Unique identifier for the country or territory record. Primary key.
International dialing prefix for the country (e.g., +1, +44, +86). Used for contact information validation and telecommunications routing.
Common short-form name of the country or territory in English. Used for display purposes in Terminal Operating System (TOS), Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS), and reporting interfaces.
Timestamp when this country record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the official currency of the country. Used for billing, tariff calculations, Currency Adjustment Factor (CAF) application, and financial reporting.
Name of the business unit or role responsible for maintaining and validating country master data. Typically Compliance & Regulatory Affairs or Master Data Management team.
Date from which this country record is effective and valid for operational use. Supports temporal validity and historical tracking of country status changes.
Date until which this country record is effective. Null if currently active. Used for historical tracking of country status changes, mergers, or dissolutions.

Status of the country with respect to Financial Action Task Force (FATF) anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing standards. Values: compliant (meets FATF standards), monitored (under increased monitoring), high_risk (identified as high-risk jurisdiction), not_assessed (not yet assessed). Impacts customer due diligence and financial transaction screening.
reference: Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Public Statements

description: Primary contact information (email, phone, or address) for the flag state maritime authority. Used for regulatory inquiries, vessel certification verification, and compliance coordination.
reference: International Maritime Organization (IMO) Flag State Directory

description: Name of the national maritime authority or flag state administration responsible for vessel registration, certification, and flag state oversight. Used for regulatory correspondence and compliance verification.
reference: International Maritime Organization (IMO) Flag State Directory

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this country is recognized as a vessel flag state. True if the country registers vessels under its flag; false otherwise. Critical for vessel registration validation and Port State Control (PSC) inspections.
reference: International Maritime Organization (IMO) Flag State Guidelines, United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)

description: Classification of the flag state based on Port State Control (PSC) performance metrics. Values: white (high-performing, low deficiency rate), grey (medium-performing, moderate deficiency rate), black (low-performing, high deficiency rate). Directly impacts vessel inspection frequency and detention risk.
reference: Paris MOU White, Grey and Black List, Tokyo MOU Performance List

description: Membership status of the country in the International Maritime Organization (IMO). Values: member (full member state), associate_member (associate member), non_member (not a member). Affects applicability of IMO conventions and compliance requirements.
reference: International Maritime Organization (IMO) Member State Directory

business_glossary_term: Indian Ocean Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Member
description: Boolean flag indicating whether the country is a member of the Indian Ocean Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control (Indian Ocean MOU). True if member; false otherwise. Determines PSC inspection regime applicability for vessels calling at ports in this country.
reference: Indian Ocean MOU on Port State Control

business_glossary_term: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 3166-1 Alpha-2 Code
description: Two-letter country code as defined by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard. Used in customs declarations, cargo manifests, and vessel registration documentation.

business_glossary_term: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 3166-1 Alpha-3 Code
description: Three-letter country code as defined by ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 standard. Commonly used in Bill of Lading (BOL), Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) messages, and Port Community System (PCS) integrations.

business_glossary_term: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 3166-1 Numeric Code
description: Three-digit numeric country code as defined by ISO 3166-1 numeric standard. Used in international trade statistics and customs systems.

business_glossary_term: International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code Compliant
description: Boolean flag indicating whether the country has implemented the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code. True if compliant; false otherwise. Critical for port security assessments and vessel clearance procedures.
Timestamp when this country record was last modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization across systems.

Boolean flag indicating whether the country has ratified the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL). True if ratified; false otherwise. Determines applicability of environmental protection and emissions standards.

Boolean flag indicating whether the country has ratified the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006. True if ratified; false otherwise. Determines applicability of seafarer labor rights and working conditions standards.
reference: International Labour Organization (ILO) Maritime Labour Convention 2006

description: Full official name of the country or territory as recognized by the United Nations and International Maritime Organization (IMO). Used in formal legal documentation, customs declarations, and compliance reporting.
reference: United Nations Terminology Database, IMO Member State Directory

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the country is a member of the Paris Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control (Paris MOU). True if member; false otherwise. Determines PSC inspection regime applicability for vessels calling at ports in this country.
reference: Paris MOU on Port State Control

description: Numeric targeting factor used by Port State Control (PSC) authorities to prioritize vessel inspections based on flag state performance. Higher values indicate higher risk and increased inspection likelihood. Range typically 0.00 to 10.00.
reference: Paris MOU, Tokyo MOU, Indian Ocean MOU Targeting Methodologies

description: Current lifecycle status of the country record. Values: active (currently in use), inactive (temporarily disabled), deprecated (no longer valid, retained for historical reference). Used to control operational visibility and data quality.
Broad geographic region classification (e.g., Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania) as defined by the United Nations geoscheme. Used for regional trade analysis and cargo routing strategies.

Date when current sanctions status became effective. Null if no sanctions are in place. Used for historical compliance tracking and audit trails.
reference: United Nations Security Council Sanctions, OFAC Sanctions Programs, EU Sanctions Map

description: Date when current sanctions are scheduled to expire or be reviewed. Null if sanctions are indefinite or no sanctions are in place. Used for forward-looking compliance planning.
reference: United Nations Security Council Sanctions, OFAC Sanctions Programs, EU Sanctions Map

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the country is currently subject to international trade sanctions or embargoes (e.g., United Nations, United States OFAC, European Union). True if sanctioned; false otherwise. Critical for trade compliance screening and cargo booking restrictions.
reference: United Nations Security Council Sanctions, OFAC Sanctions Programs, EU Sanctions Map

business_glossary_term: Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) Convention Ratified
description: Boolean flag indicating whether the country has ratified the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS). True if ratified; false otherwise. Determines applicability of SOLAS safety requirements for vessels flagged or calling at ports in this country.

Sub-regional classification within the broader region (e.g., Eastern Asia, Western Europe, Southern Africa) as defined by the United Nations geoscheme. Supports granular trade flow analysis and vessel routing optimization.

Boolean flag indicating whether the country is a member of the Tokyo Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control (Tokyo MOU). True if member; false otherwise. Determines PSC inspection regime applicability for vessels calling at ports in this country.
reference: Tokyo MOU on Port State Control

description: Comma-separated list of trade agreement codes applicable to this country (e.g., USMCA, EU, ASEAN, CPTPP, RCEP). Used to determine preferential tariff rates, customs duty exemptions, and Terminal Handling Charge (THC) adjustments.
reference: World Trade Organization (WTO) Regional Trade Agreements Database

business_glossary_term: United Nations Code for Trade and Transport Locations (UN/LOCODE) Prefix
description: Two-letter country prefix used in UN/LOCODE location codes. Matches ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Used to construct full UN/LOCODE identifiers for ports and inland terminals within this country.
reference: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) UN/LOCODE

description: Boolean flag indicating whether the country is a member of the World Customs Organization (WCO). True if member; false otherwise. Affects customs clearance procedures, Harmonized System (HS) Code usage, and trade facilitation standards.
Unique identifier for the equipment type record. Primary key for the equipment type master data entity.

Degree of automation for the equipment type. Values: manual (operator-controlled with no automation), semi_automated (operator-assisted with automated functions such as auto-positioning or collision avoidance), fully_automated (autonomous operation with remote monitoring such as AutoRTG, AutoASC, AGV). Impacts workforce planning, training requirements, and operational efficiency metrics.
reference: IAPH Smart Port Guidelines, NAVIS N4 Automation Configuration

description: Frequency of mandatory certification or statutory inspection for the equipment type expressed in months. Typical values: 12 months for lifting equipment SWL certificates, 24 months for pressure vessel inspections. Null if certification_required_flag is False.
reference: SOLAS Chapter VI Regulation 5, ISO 9927 Cranes - Inspections, National Maritime Safety Authority Regulations

description: Indicates whether the equipment type requires periodic certification or inspection by a competent authority or third-party surveyor. True for lifting equipment requiring SWL certificates, pressure vessels, cranes subject to statutory inspection. False for equipment without regulatory certification requirements.
reference: SOLAS Chapter VI Regulation 5, ISO 9927 Cranes - Inspections, Port State Control (PSC) Guidelines

description: Indicates whether the equipment type is equipped with collision avoidance or anti-collision systems. True for equipment with radar, lidar, proximity sensors, or automated braking systems to prevent collisions with other equipment, containers, or personnel. False for equipment without collision avoidance capability.
reference: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety, IAPH Smart Port Safety Guidelines

description: Timestamp when this equipment type record was first created in the master data system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601 Date and Time Format, DAMA-DMBOK Data Lineage

description: Name or identifier of the business unit or role responsible for maintaining and governing this equipment type master data. Typically Asset Management, Engineering, or Terminal Operations. Used for data quality accountability and change request routing.
reference: ISO 8000 Data Quality, DAMA-DMBOK Data Governance

description: Date from which this equipment type classification becomes effective and valid for use in operational systems. Used for managing equipment type lifecycle and supporting historical reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

Date until which this equipment type classification remains valid. Null for currently active equipment types. Populated when an equipment type is retired, superseded, or reclassified. Used for managing equipment type lifecycle and supporting historical reporting. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

Applicable emissions standard or tier classification for the equipment type. Examples: EPA Tier 3, EPA Tier 4 Final, Euro Stage V, IMO Tier II, IMO Tier III. Relevant for diesel-powered equipment and harbour tugs. Null for electric or manual equipment.
reference: MARPOL Annex VI Air Pollution, EPA Nonroad Diesel Emission Standards, EMS Emissions Tracking

description: Indicates whether the equipment type is subject to environmental compliance monitoring and reporting requirements. True for diesel-powered equipment subject to emissions tracking (MARPOL Annex VI), noise monitoring, or fuel consumption reporting. False for equipment with no environmental compliance obligations.
reference: MARPOL Annex VI Air Pollution, ISO 14001 Environmental Management, EMS Emissions Tracking

description: Standardized alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the equipment type across all port systems. Used as the business key for equipment classification in Terminal Operating System (TOS), asset registry, and maintenance planning systems.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management, NAVIS N4 Equipment Type Master

description: Full descriptive name of the equipment type. Human-readable label used in operational displays, reports, and user interfaces.

Current lifecycle status of the equipment type master record. business_glossary_term: Fuel Consumption in Litres per Hour
description: Average fuel consumption rate for diesel-powered equipment types expressed in litres per hour under normal operating conditions. Used for operational cost estimation, fuel budgeting, and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions calculations. Null for electric, battery, or manual equipment.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management, EMS Emissions Tracking

business_glossary_term: Global Positioning System (GPS) Tracking Enabled Flag
description: Indicates whether the equipment type is equipped with GPS (Global Positioning System) tracking capability for real-time location monitoring. True for mobile equipment with GPS transponders used in yard management, dispatch optimization, and asset visibility. False for stationary equipment or equipment without GPS.
reference: ISO 19116 Geographic Information Positioning Services, NAVIS N4 Equipment Tracking

business_glossary_term: Internet of Things (IoT) Sensor Enabled Flag
description: Indicates whether the equipment type is equipped with IoT (Internet of Things) sensors for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. True for equipment with sensors monitoring temperature, vibration, oil quality, load stress, or other operational parameters. False for equipment without IoT sensor integration.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management, Maximo Asset Management IoT Integration

description: Timestamp when this equipment type record was last updated or modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization across systems. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601 Date and Time Format, DAMA-DMBOK Data Lineage

description: Maximum vertical lift height capability of the equipment type in metres. Relevant for cranes, reach stackers, and stacking equipment. Determines container stacking height and vessel reach capability. Null for equipment without lift capability.
reference: ISO 9927 Cranes - Inspections, NAVIS N4 Yard Planning Parameters

description: Standard preventive maintenance interval for the equipment type expressed in operating hours. Defines the frequency of scheduled maintenance activities based on OEM recommendations. Used by Maximo Asset Management for work order scheduling and maintenance planning.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management, Maximo Asset Management Preventive Maintenance Schedule

description: Applicable maintenance standard or framework governing the equipment type. Examples: OEM-specific maintenance program, ISO 55000 Asset Management, SOLAS inspection requirements, Port State Control (PSC) standards, manufacturer service bulletins. References the authoritative source for maintenance procedures and intervals.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management, SOLAS Chapter I Regulation 6, Maximo Asset Management Standards Library

description: Name of the original equipment manufacturer (OEM). Used for warranty tracking, spare parts sourcing, and maintenance standard alignment.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management, Maximo Asset Management OEM Reference

description: Manufacturer model number or designation for this equipment type. Links to OEM technical specifications, parts catalogs, and maintenance manuals.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management, Maximo Asset Management Model Master

description: Standard productivity rate for the equipment type expressed as container moves per hour under normal operating conditions. Key Performance Indicator (KPI) for equipment performance benchmarking, berth planning, and Service Level Agreement (SLA) commitments. Relevant for cranes and container handling equipment. Null for non-handling equipment.
reference: IAPH Port Performance Indicators, NAVIS N4 Productivity Standards

business_glossary_term: Operational Speed in Kilometres per Hour (km/h)
description: Maximum operational travel speed of mobile equipment in kilometres per hour. Used for cycle time calculations, yard planning, and safety zone definitions. Relevant for terminal tractors, straddle carriers, reach stackers, AGVs, and harbour tugs. Null for stationary equipment.
reference: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety, NAVIS N4 Dispatch Planning

description: Type of operator certification or licence required to operate this equipment type. Examples: Crane Operator Licence (STS/RTG/ASC), Forklift Operator Certificate, Heavy Vehicle Licence, Marine Pilot Licence, IMDG Dangerous Goods Handling Certificate. Null for equipment not requiring operator certification. Used by Oracle HCM Cloud for workforce competency management and training planning.
reference: ILO Maritime Labour Convention, ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety, Oracle HCM Competency Management

description: Maximum horizontal reach or outreach distance of the equipment type in metres. Critical specification for Ship-to-Shore (STS) cranes and Quay Cranes (QC) to determine vessel size compatibility and berth planning. Null for equipment without reach capability.
reference: ISO 9927 Cranes - Inspections, NAVIS N4 Berth Planning Parameters

description: Average electrical power consumption for electric-powered equipment types expressed in kilowatts (kW) under normal operating conditions. Used for energy cost estimation, electrical infrastructure planning, and carbon footprint calculations. Null for diesel or manual equipment.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management, EMS Energy Monitoring

description: Primary power source or propulsion type for the equipment. Values: electric (grid-powered or e-RTG), diesel (internal combustion engine), hybrid (diesel-electric or dual-mode), battery (battery-electric or AGV), manual (non-powered equipment). Critical for environmental reporting (GHG emissions), energy management, and infrastructure planning (charging stations, fuel depots).
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management, MARPOL Annex VI Air Pollution, EMS Emissions Tracking

description: Free-text field for additional notes, special handling instructions, or contextual information about the equipment type that does not fit structured fields. Examples: phase-out plans, replacement recommendations, operational constraints, vendor support notes.

Indicates whether the equipment type is equipped with RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology for automated tracking and identification. True for equipment with onboard RFID readers or tags used in automated gate operations, yard management, or asset tracking. False for equipment without RFID capability.
reference: ISO 18000 RFID Standards, NAVIS N4 RFID Integration

description: Rail span or track gauge distance for rail-mounted equipment types (RTG, ASC, rail-mounted gantry cranes) in metres. Defines the width of the equipment footprint and yard lane compatibility. Null for non-rail-mounted equipment.
reference: ISO 9927 Cranes - Inspections, NAVIS N4 Yard Configuration

business_glossary_term: Safe Working Load (SWL) Rating in Tonnes
description: Maximum safe working load capacity of the equipment type expressed in metric tonnes. Critical for operational planning, load distribution, and safety compliance. Applies primarily to lifting equipment (cranes, reach stackers, forklifts). Null for non-lifting equipment.
reference: SOLAS Chapter VI Regulation 5, ISO 9927 Cranes - Inspections, Maximo Asset Management SWL Certificate

description: Container handling capacity of the equipment type expressed in TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Units). Represents the number of TEU the equipment can handle or transport in a single operation. Relevant for container handling equipment, terminal tractors, and AGVs. Null for non-container-handling equipment.
reference: ISO 668 Freight Containers Classification, NAVIS N4 Equipment Capacity

description: Unique identifier for the port location record. Primary key for the port_location entity.

Distance in meters between mooring bollards along the berth or quay. Critical for vessel mooring planning and safe berthing operations. Applicable to berth and quay locations.

business_glossary_term: Bollard Safe Working Load (SWL) in Tonnes
description: Safe Working Load (SWL) of mooring bollards at this location, measured in metric tonnes. Defines the maximum safe mooring line tension. Applicable to berth and quay locations.
reference: PIANC Mooring Equipment Guidelines; ISO 3913 Shipbuilding Bollards

description: Date when the location was officially commissioned and became operational. Marks the start of the location's active lifecycle. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: AVEVA Marine Engineering Project Lifecycle; Asset Management Standards

business_glossary_term: Container Yard Capacity in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEU)
description: Total container storage capacity of the yard location measured in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEU). Applicable to Container Yard (CY) and container stacking locations.
reference: ISO 668 Container Classification; NAVIS N4 Yard Capacity Planning
