description: The NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System work queue identifier associated with this roster assignment, linking the labour plan to specific container handling or vessel operations tasks in the TOS.
reference: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System Labour Planning; TOPS Expert Terminal Operating System

description: The pay rate multiplier applied to overtime shift assignments (e.g., 1.5 for time-and-a-half, 2.0 for double time). Used in payroll calculation for overtime and call-out shifts. Classified as confidential.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Payroll; SAP S/4HANA HR; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: The pay grade or salary band code applicable to the employee for this roster assignment, determining the base pay rate for payroll processing. Classified as confidential business data.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Payroll; SAP S/4HANA HR; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: The last calendar date of the roster planning period for which this assignment is valid. Together with roster_period_start_date, defines the scheduling window.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: The first calendar date of the roster planning period for which this assignment is valid. Used to define the scheduling window for advance labour planning aligned to vessel call schedules.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: The total planned working duration of the shift in decimal hours, excluding break entitlements. Used for payroll calculation, MLC maximum hours of work compliance, and labour cost forecasting.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: The planned date and time at which the employee's shift is scheduled to conclude. Used together with planned_start_time for MLC rest hour compliance and shift duration calculations.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: The planned date and time at which the employee's shift is scheduled to commence. Used for MLC rest hour compliance calculations and labour deployment planning.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: The actual number of rest hours recorded between the previous shift end and this shift's planned start time. Used to validate MLC minimum rest hour compliance before publishing the roster.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Port State Control (PSC) Inspection Requirements

description: The date and time at which the roster was published and made available to employees. Supports advance notice compliance requirements under enterprise agreements and MLC provisions.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: Externally-known business identifier for the roster record, used in workforce planning communications, MLC compliance reporting, and integration with Oracle HCM Cloud and SAP HR. Format: RST-YYYY-NNNNNN.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Scheduling; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: Current lifecycle state of the roster assignment. Draft indicates initial planning; published indicates the roster has been released to employees; confirmed indicates employee acknowledgement; cancelled indicates the assignment was withdrawn; superseded indicates replaced by a revised roster.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006

description: Classification of the shift assignment type. Regular denotes standard scheduled work; overtime denotes hours beyond standard; standby denotes on-call availability; call_out denotes unplanned emergency activation; training denotes scheduled training shifts; rest denotes mandatory MLC rest periods. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: regular|overtime|standby|call_out|training|rest — promote to reference product]
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: The contracted or target number of minutes within which the assigned employee or gang must be ready and deployed at the designated work location after shift commencement. Supports Key Performance Indicator (KPI) measurement for vessel turnaround SLA compliance.
reference: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; IAPH Port Performance Standards; SLA Management

description: Code identifying the operational system of record from which this roster record originated. Supports data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer. Values: ORACLE_HCM (Oracle HCM Cloud), NAVIS_N4 (NAVIS N4 Labour Planning), SAP_HR (SAP S/4HANA HR), MANUAL (manually entered).
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud; NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: The native record identifier from the originating operational system (Oracle HCM Cloud, NAVIS N4, or SAP HR) for this roster entry. Enables reconciliation and traceability back to the system of record.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud; NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Reference number linking this roster assignment to a specific operational work order in NAVIS N4 or Maximo, such as a cargo loading/discharge operation or equipment maintenance task.
reference: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; Maximo Asset Management Work Orders

description: Primary key for shift_pattern

Foreign key linking to masterdata.port_location. Business justification: Shift patterns are location-specific (berth operations differ from yard operations in timing and fatigue risk). FK supports MLC rest hour compliance by location, fatigue management, and shift planning

Name or code of the port department or operational division to which this shift pattern applies (e.g., 'Terminal Operations', 'Marine Services', 'Security', 'Yard Operations', 'Gate Operations', 'Administration'). Supports department-level workforce planning and reporting.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; SAP S/4HANA HR Organisational Management

description: Workflow approval status of the shift pattern, particularly relevant for new or modified shift patterns requiring HR, union, or MLC compliance sign-off before activation. Supports governance and change management processes.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; ILO Maritime Labour Convention; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Name or employee identifier of the HR manager or authorised officer who approved this shift pattern for operational use. Supports audit trail requirements for MLC compliance and enterprise governance.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006; Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules

description: Date on which this shift pattern received final approval for operational use. Supports audit trail and MLC compliance documentation requirements.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006; Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules

description: Number of discrete break periods scheduled within the shift pattern. Supports detailed roster planning and MLC rest hour compliance verification where minimum break frequency is mandated.

Total scheduled break entitlement in minutes for the shift pattern. Includes all meal and rest breaks. Distinguishing paid vs unpaid breaks is captured in is_break_paid flag. Used for MLC rest hour compliance and payroll deduction calculations.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: Timestamp when this shift pattern record was first created in the data platform. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security; Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules

description: Comma-separated list of days on which this shift pattern is scheduled (e.g., 'MON,TUE,WED,THU,FRI' for weekdays; 'SAT,SUN' for weekends; 'MON,TUE,WED,THU,FRI,SAT,SUN' for 7-day operations). Supports roster generation and weekend/public holiday penalty rate identification.

Total scheduled duration of the shift in minutes, inclusive of paid breaks but exclusive of unpaid breaks. Represents the principal quantitative fact of the shift pattern. Used for payroll hours calculation, MLC maximum hours of work compliance, and workforce capacity planning.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules

description: Date from which this shift pattern is valid and available for roster assignment. Supports temporal versioning of shift patterns to accommodate enterprise award changes, MLC updates, or operational restructuring.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006

description: Date after which this shift pattern is no longer valid for new roster assignments. Null indicates the shift pattern is open-ended and currently active. Supports temporal versioning and historical roster analysis.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006

description: Scheduled end time of the shift in HH:MM (24-hour) format, independent of date. For overnight shifts where end_time is earlier than start_time, the shift is understood to span midnight. Used in roster generation, time-attendance validation, and overtime calculation.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: Code referencing the enterprise bargaining agreement or industrial award under which this shift pattern is defined (e.g., 'MUA-EBA-2023', 'AMOU-AWARD-2022'). Ensures payroll and rostering compliance with applicable industrial instruments for maritime and port workers.
reference: ILO Maritime Labour Convention; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Numeric fatigue risk score assigned to this shift pattern based on shift timing, duration, and rotation frequency. Higher values indicate greater fatigue risk. Used in MLC compliance monitoring, OHS risk management, and roster optimisation to minimise fatigue-related incidents in safety-critical port operations.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; National Maritime Safety Authority

business_glossary_term: Oracle Human Capital Management (HCM) Work Schedule ID
description: Source system identifier for the corresponding Work Schedule record in Oracle HCM Cloud. Enables bi-directional traceability between the Silver Layer data product and the operational system of record for reconciliation and change management.
Indicates whether the scheduled break entitlement for this shift pattern is paid (True) or unpaid (False). Determines whether break_duration_minutes is deducted from paid_hours in payroll processing.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Indicates whether the shift pattern spans midnight (True) or is contained within a single calendar day (False). Used in roster date calculations, night shift penalty rate application, and MLC rest hour tracking across calendar day boundaries.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules

description: Indicates whether this shift pattern is scheduled to operate on public holidays (True) or is suspended on public holidays (False). Drives public holiday penalty rate application in payroll and supports port operational continuity planning for 24/7 terminal operations.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: Workforce job family or occupational group for which this shift pattern is designed (e.g., 'Stevedore Gang', 'Equipment Operator', 'Marine Pilot', 'Security Officer', 'Crane Operator', 'Administrative'). Supports targeted roster assignment and competency-based scheduling.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Workforce Management; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: Maximum number of personnel that can be rostered under this shift pattern, constrained by equipment capacity, berth space, or operational safety limits. Used in workforce scheduling to prevent over-allocation and manage OPEX.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Workforce Management; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety

description: Minimum number of personnel required to be rostered under this shift pattern to meet safe operational standards and SLA commitments. Used in workforce capacity planning, gang allocation for stevedore operations, and OHS compliance validation.
reference: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; National Maritime Safety Authority; Oracle HCM Cloud Workforce Management

description: Indicates whether this shift pattern has been validated as compliant with all applicable Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 rest hour and maximum hours of work requirements (True) or has identified non-compliance issues (False). Supports MLC audit readiness and Port State Control (PSC) inspection preparation.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Port State Control (PSC) Authorities; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

business_glossary_term: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) Maximum Hours of Work Per Day
description: Maximum hours of work permitted per 24-hour period under the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 for this shift pattern. Standard MLC limit is 14 hours. Used in compliance validation to ensure shift assignments do not breach MLC rest hour requirements.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3 Standard A2.3 paragraph 5(a)

business_glossary_term: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) Maximum Hours of Work Per Week
description: Maximum hours of work permitted per 7-day period under the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 for this shift pattern. Standard MLC limit is 72 hours. Used in weekly compliance reporting and roster validation.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3 Standard A2.3 paragraph 5(a)

business_glossary_term: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) Minimum Rest Hours Per Day
description: Minimum hours of rest required per 24-hour period under the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 for this shift pattern. Standard MLC minimum is 10 hours. Used in compliance validation to ensure adequate rest between consecutive shift assignments.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3 Standard A2.3 paragraph 5(b)

business_glossary_term: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) Minimum Rest Hours Per Week
description: Minimum hours of rest required per 7-day period under the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 for this shift pattern. Standard MLC minimum is 77 hours. Used in weekly MLC compliance reporting submitted to Port State Control (PSC) authorities.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3 Standard A2.3 paragraph 5(b); Port State Control (PSC) Authorities

business_glossary_term: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Risk Level
description: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) risk classification assigned to this shift pattern based on time-of-day, operational environment, and task type. Drives mandatory safety briefing requirements, PPE specifications, and incident reporting thresholds. Aligns with ISO 45001 risk assessment framework.
reference: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; National Maritime Safety Authority; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: Number of hours worked within this shift pattern beyond which overtime rates apply. Used in payroll processing to automatically trigger overtime rate calculations in Oracle HCM Cloud and SAP S/4HANA HR.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Payroll; SAP S/4HANA HR; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.2

description: Number of hours for which the employee is remunerated under this shift pattern, after deducting unpaid break entitlements from total duration. Used as the basis for payroll processing in SAP S/4HANA HR and Oracle HCM Cloud Payroll.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Payroll; SAP S/4HANA HR; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.2

description: Payroll penalty rate code applicable to this shift pattern, referencing the enterprise pay rate schedule in SAP S/4HANA HR (e.g., 'NIGHT-1.5X', 'WKND-2X', 'PH-2.5X', 'STD-1X'). Drives automated payroll calculation for shift-based penalty loadings.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll; Oracle HCM Cloud Payroll; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: Comma-separated list of competency certification codes required for personnel assigned to this shift pattern (e.g., 'STCW,ISPS,RTG-OPS,STS-CRANE'). Used in competency-based scheduling to ensure only qualified personnel are rostered. References the workforce competency certification register.
reference: STCW Convention; ISPS Code Administration; IMO; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: Number of calendar days in the full rotation cycle for rotating shift patterns (e.g., 7 for weekly rotation, 14 for fortnightly, 28 for 4-week cycle). Null for non-rotating shift types. Used in roster generation and long-term workforce planning.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: Ordinal position of this shift pattern within a rotation cycle (e.g., 1 = first leg, 2 = second leg). Used to sequence multiple shift_pattern records that together form a complete rotating roster cycle. Null for non-rotating shift types.

SAP S/4HANA HR work schedule variant code corresponding to this shift pattern, used for payroll time evaluation and absence/attendance management. Enables cross-system alignment between Oracle HCM Cloud roster data and SAP payroll processing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Time Management; SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: Broad time-of-day category of the shift pattern used for workforce planning, penalty rate determination, and MLC rest hour compliance reporting. 'day' typically covers 06:00–18:00; 'afternoon' covers 14:00–22:00; 'night' covers 22:00–06:00; 'early_morning' covers 04:00–12:00; 'rotating' covers patterns that cycle across categories.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the shift pattern (e.g., DAY-01, NIGHT-03, STBY-AM). Used as the business key across Oracle HCM Cloud, SAP HR, and NAVIS N4 for cross-system referencing.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Free-text description providing additional context about the shift pattern, including operational purpose, special conditions, applicable vessel operations, or notes on MLC compliance exceptions. Supports business user understanding and documentation.
Human-readable name of the shift pattern (e.g., 'Day Shift', 'Night Shift', 'Afternoon Rotating', 'Marine Pilot Standby'). Used in rosters, payroll reports, and workforce scheduling displays.

Current lifecycle status of the shift pattern record. 'active' indicates available for roster assignment; 'inactive' indicates temporarily suspended; 'draft' indicates pending approval; 'under_review' indicates subject to MLC or award compliance review; 'retired' indicates permanently decommissioned.

Classification of the shift pattern by operational nature. 'regular' covers standard scheduled shifts; 'overtime' covers extended hours beyond standard; 'standby' covers on-call availability; 'call_out' covers unplanned emergency activation; 'rotating' covers cyclically alternating shifts; 'split' covers shifts with a significant mid-shift break. Drives payroll rate application and MLC rest hour compliance checks.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules

description: Minimum notice period in minutes required to activate an employee from standby to active duty under this shift pattern. Applicable only to standby and call-out shift types. Used in operational planning for vessel arrival response and emergency port operations.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; ISPS Code Administration

description: Scheduled start time of the shift in HH:MM (24-hour) format, independent of date. Used in roster generation, time-attendance validation, and overtime calculation. For rotating shifts, represents the start time of the primary rotation leg.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: Timestamp when this shift pattern record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking, data quality monitoring, and audit trail requirements. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security; Oracle HCM Cloud Work Schedules

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each time and attendance record in the port workforce management system. Primary key for this entity.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance Module; SAP S/4HANA HR Module

description: Foreign key linking to infrastructure.berth. Business justification: Time tracking at berth level enables accurate costing per berth, productivity measurement, and labor cost allocation to vessel calls. Essential for berth utilization analysis and operational KPIs.

Reference to the vessel operation or port call to which the employee's shift labour was allocated. Applicable for stevedores, marine pilots, mooring gangs, and other vessel-facing roles. Enables vessel-level labour cost attribution.
reference: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; TOPS Expert TOS; IAPH Port Labour Standards

description: Reference to the stevedore gang or work crew to which the employee was assigned during this shift. Applicable for stevedores, equipment operators, and dock workers performing cargo handling operations. Used for gang-level productivity and labour cost analysis.
reference: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; IAPH Port Labour Standards

description: Foreign key linking to workforce.leave_request. Business justification: When an employee is absent, the time_attendance record can reference the approved leave_request. This is an optional (nullable) relationship - not all absences have formal leave requests. Enables link
Reference to the SAP HR payroll run in which this attendance record was processed. Populated once payroll_processed = True. Enables traceability between attendance records and payroll outputs.

Foreign key linking to masterdata.port_location. Business justification: Attendance is recorded at specific locations (gate entry, berth, yard) for time tracking, payroll cost allocation by location, and ISPS security compliance. FK enables location-based labor cost report

Code identifying the employee's job role or position during this shift (e.g., STEVEDORE, QC-OPERATOR, MARINE-PILOT, SECURITY-OFFICER, ADMIN). Used for role-based pay rate application and workforce composition reporting.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Workforce Management; SAP S/4HANA HR; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: Reference to the employee whose time and attendance is being recorded. Links to the workforce employee master record in Oracle HCM Cloud.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Workforce Management; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Foreign key linking to workforce.roster. Business justification: time_attendance records actual attendance for a rostered shift. The roster is the plan, time_attendance is the actuals. This FK links actual time worked to the planned roster entry, enabling plan vs.
Reference to the scheduled shift assignment for which this attendance record applies. Links to the shift scheduling master.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance Module

description: Reference to the port terminal or facility where the employee worked during this shift. Supports multi-terminal port operations where employees may be deployed across different terminals.
reference: NAVIS N4 Terminal Operating System; PMIS Port Management Information System

description: Classification of the reason for employee absence when attendance_status is 'absent'. Drives leave balance deduction and payroll treatment in Oracle HCM Cloud and SAP HR. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: annual_leave|sick_leave|unpaid_leave|public_holiday|maternity_paternity|training|compassionate|jury_duty|medical_appointment|suspension — promote to reference product]
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.4; ILO Convention; Oracle HCM Cloud

description: Free-text description of the reason for any manual amendment or correction to this attendance record (e.g., system outage, RFID reader failure, missed clock-out). Required when entry_method is 'manual' or 'supervisor_entry' for audit trail purposes.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; SAP S/4HANA HR; MLC 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: Workflow approval status of the time and attendance record. Records must be approved by a supervisor before being submitted to payroll. Pending = awaiting review; Approved = confirmed for payroll; Rejected = returned for correction; Disputed = under formal dispute.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: The date and time when the supervisor approved or rejected this attendance record. Part of the payroll audit trail and MLC compliance documentation.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006

description: The calendar date for which this time and attendance record applies. Used for daily payroll calculation, MLC rest hour compliance monitoring, and workforce reporting.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Oracle HCM Cloud

description: Current attendance status of the employee for the shift. Indicates whether the employee was present, absent, arrived late, departed early, or partially attended. Critical for payroll deduction and MLC compliance reporting.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006; Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance

description: Indicates whether the employee's identity was verified via biometric authentication (fingerprint, facial recognition) at clock-in or gate entry. True = biometric verification completed; False = RFID-only or manual entry. Supports ISPS security compliance and payroll fraud prevention.
reference: ISPS Code Part A; ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety; Oracle HCM Cloud

description: Total break time in minutes taken by the employee during the shift. Captured from RFID or biometric break-room scan data. Used to compute net hours worked for payroll and MLC rest hour compliance.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; ILO Maritime Labour Convention

description: The timestamp when the employee returned from their scheduled break period. Used together with break_start_timestamp to calculate total break duration and net productive hours.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Oracle HCM Cloud

description: The timestamp when the employee commenced their scheduled break period during the shift. Used to calculate net working hours and verify MLC minimum rest period compliance.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Oracle HCM Cloud

description: The exact date and time the employee clocked in at the start of their shift, captured via RFID badge scan or biometric verification at the terminal gate or facility entry point. Principal business event timestamp for this record.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: The exact date and time the employee clocked out at the end of their shift, captured via RFID badge scan or biometric verification. Used to calculate total hours worked and overtime.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3

description: SAP CO cost center code to which the employee's worked hours are charged for financial accounting and OPEX allocation. Enables labour cost attribution by terminal operation, department, or project.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO Controlling Module; IAPH Port Finance Standards

description: The date and time when this time and attendance record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data governance and compliance purposes.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud; SAP S/4HANA HR; ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security

description: Number of minutes the employee departed before the scheduled shift end time. Zero if departed on time or later. Used for attendance discipline tracking and payroll deduction calculation.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: The method by which the clock-in/clock-out time was captured. RFID scan = automated badge reader; Biometric = fingerprint/facial recognition; Manual = supervisor or HR manual entry; Mobile app = employee self-service; Supervisor entry = entered by line manager.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; ISPS Code

description: The timestamp when the employee physically entered the port terminal through the security gate, captured from NAVIS N4 Gate Operations or ISPS-compliant access control system. May differ from clock_in_timestamp if the employee entered the terminal before clocking in.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 16; NAVIS N4 Gate Operations; IMO MSC/Circ.1192

description: The timestamp when the employee physically exited the port terminal through the security gate. Used for ISPS security compliance, access duration tracking, and cross-referencing with clock-out data.
reference: ISPS Code Part A Section 16; NAVIS N4 Gate Operations; IMO MSC/Circ.1192

description: Total net hours worked by the employee during the shift, calculated as (clock_out - clock_in) minus break_duration_minutes. Expressed in decimal hours. Feeds SAP HR payroll calculation and MLC rest hour compliance monitoring.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: Indicates whether the attendance date falls on a public holiday. True = public holiday; False = regular working day. Drives public holiday pay rate multiplier application in SAP HR payroll.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; ILO

description: Number of minutes the employee arrived late relative to the scheduled shift start time. Zero if on time or early. Used for attendance discipline tracking, payroll deduction calculation, and KPI reporting on workforce punctuality.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

business_glossary_term: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) Rest Hours Compliance Flag
description: Indicates whether the employee's rest hours between this shift and the previous shift meet the MLC 2006 minimum rest period requirements (minimum 10 hours rest in any 24-hour period; minimum 77 hours rest in any 7-day period). True = compliant; False = potential MLC violation requiring review.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3 Standard A2.3; IMO

description: Number of hours worked beyond the standard shift duration, expressed in decimal hours. Used for overtime pay calculation in SAP HR payroll and for MLC maximum hours of work compliance monitoring.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll

description: Identifier for the payroll period (e.g., 2024-W23, 2024-M06) to which this attendance record belongs. Used to group attendance records for payroll run processing in SAP HR.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll Module; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.2

description: Indicates whether this attendance record has been included in a payroll run and processed in SAP HR. True = included in payroll; False = pending payroll processing. Prevents double-counting in payroll runs.
reference: SAP S/4HANA HR Payroll Module; Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.2

description: Number of hours of rest the employee had between the end of their previous shift and the start of this shift. Critical for MLC 2006 Regulation 2.3 compliance monitoring — minimum 10 hours rest required in any 24-hour period.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Standard A2.3; National Maritime Safety Authority

description: The unique RFID badge identifier used by the employee to clock in/out and access the terminal. Captured from RFID reader scan events. Used to verify identity and link physical access events to attendance records.
reference: ISPS Code; ISO 18000 RFID Standards; NAVIS N4 Gate Operations

description: The planned end time of the employee's shift as per the shift schedule. Used to calculate early departure and compare against actual clock-out time.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: The planned start time of the employee's shift as per the shift schedule. Used to calculate lateness and compare against actual clock-in time for attendance compliance.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud Time and Attendance; SAP S/4HANA HR

description: Classification of the shift pattern worked by the employee. Port operations run 24/7 across day, afternoon, and night shifts. Used for shift differential pay calculation and MLC rest hour compliance monitoring.
reference: Maritime Labour Convention (MLC) 2006 Regulation 2.3; Oracle HCM Cloud

description: The native record identifier from the originating source system (Oracle HCM Cloud, SAP HR, or NAVIS N4). Used for data lineage tracing, reconciliation, and deduplication in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud; SAP S/4HANA HR; NAVIS N4

description: The date and time when this time and attendance record was last modified. Used to track amendments, corrections, and approval workflow updates for audit trail purposes.
reference: Oracle HCM Cloud; SAP S/4HANA HR; ISO 28000 Supply Chain Security

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each competency record in the master catalogue. Primary key for the competency data product.

Foreign key linking to masterdata.equipment_type. Business justification: Competencies authorize operation of specific equipment types (crane operator, RTG driver). FK enables competency-equipment matching for deployment, certification tracking, workforce capability plannin

Foreign key linking to masterdata.imdg_class. Business justification: Dangerous goods competencies are IMDG class-specific (Class 1 explosives, Class 2 gases). FK enables DG handling authorization, gang assignment validation for hazmat cargo, and IMDG Code compliance tr

Foreign key linking to masterdata.vessel_type. Business justification: Competencies apply to vessel types (STCW endorsements, pilot licenses for specific vessel classes). FK enables crew qualification verification, pilot dispatch validation, and maritime training complia

Port workforce job family or occupational group for which this competency is relevant (e.g., 'Marine Pilot', 'Stevedore', 'Equipment Operator', 'Port Security Officer', 'Harbour Master'). Supports role-based competency gap analysis and workforce planning. reference: Oracle HCM Cloud - Job Families; ILO MLC 2006; IAPH Workforce Standards

description: Name of the approved training institution or provider authorised by the issuing authority to deliver training for this competency (e.g., 'Australian Maritime College', 'Port Authority Training Centre'). Ensures workforce training is conducted through recognised providers.
